subject: Perf-canary alerting policy review (paging volume + phased rollout)
related_links: Linear: ENG-2848 (Alert routing: page SRE for initial triage, auto-assign Runtime when confirmed)
Jira: INT-3330 (Create PagerDuty service/routing rule for perf regression alerts)
body:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Tomáš Novák <tomas.novak@redwoodinference.com>, Allison Grant <allison.grant@redwoodinference.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, Jan 10, 2026 at 5:42 PM PST
Subject: Perf-canary alerting policy review (paging volume + phased rollout)

Team,

I reviewed the current draft alert rules + the policy notes floating around ENG-2848. I’m supportive of paging for real regressions, but I’m worried we’re going to page too often in the first 2–3 weeks (warmup effects, deploy windows, baseline drift, GPU heterogeneity).

Proposal for v1 rollout:

1) Phased rollout + ticket-first mode
- Week 1: run detectors in “ticket-only” (no PD paging) for us-east + 2–3 models. Auto-file Jira (or Linear) + post to #eng-oncall with context.
- Week 2: enable paging only for “critical” severity in the same limited scope.
- Expand scope only after we backtest alert volume and tune thresholds.

2) Severity mapping (suggestion)
- WARN (ticket/Slack): p95 latency regression > 10% vs baseline sustained 30m OR tokens/sec drop > 8% sustained 30m.
- CRITICAL (page): p95 latency regression > 15% sustained 20m OR tokens/sec drop > 12% sustained 20m.
- Page only if minimum sample size is met (e.g., N>=200 requests in window per slice). I don’t want pages off tiny samples.

3) Gating + suppression
- Hard suppress during known deploy windows (runtime rollout events) + first ~10m after a canary runner restart (cache priming / cold starts).
- Alert payload must include “suppression reason” when suppressed (so we can see we didn’t just miss it).

4) Dedup/grouping keys
- Paging dedup key should be coarse enough to avoid storms: model + region + metric (latency vs tps) + severity.
- Debug context can include gpu_sku/runtime_build/scheduler_mode, but don’t group pages by those dimensions.

Ask:
- Mateo: are you OK with ticket-first for the initial week? (I know Runtime wants fast signal, but pager fatigue will kill adoption.)
- Allison/Logan: can we confirm that the label schema supports the above (keeping cardinality sane) while still attaching GPU SKU/build in payload?
- Rafael/Tomáš: can you sanity check the PD + incident-bot flow for ticket-first and then critical paging?

If folks agree, I’ll write this into the Confluence alert policy page and reference it in the runbook.

Sean
—
Sean Gallagher
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference



From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Tomáš Novák <tomas.novak@redwoodinference.com>, Allison Grant <allison.grant@redwoodinference.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, Jan 11, 2026 at 9:06 AM PST
Subject: Re: Perf-canary alerting policy review (paging volume + phased rollout)

Sean,

Yes — I’m fine with ticket-first in week 1 as long as:
- we still get a high-signal notification in #eng-oncall with a clear “this would have paged” marker, and
- we’re capturing enough context to attribute quickly (runtime_build, scheduler_mode, kernel id/fallback reason, gpu_sku).

On thresholds, I’d prefer we page only on CRITICAL *and* only when we see the regression across at least two consecutive windows (to reduce noise), unless it’s a really large step function.

One nuance: tokens/sec can be noisy if the scheduler mixes traffic. If we’re pinning scheduler config for canary (as discussed), then I’m good with using tps in severity mapping.

Let’s do:
- Week 1 ticket-first + backtest.
- Week 2 page on CRITICAL only.
- Expand after we see <1 page/day expected.

Thanks,
Mateo



From: Allison Grant <allison.grant@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Tomáš Novák <tomas.novak@redwoodinference.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, Jan 11, 2026 at 11:22 AM PST
Subject: Re: Perf-canary alerting policy review (paging volume + phased rollout)

+1 to ticket-first.

On schema/cardinality:
- We should NOT allow gpu_sku and runtime_build as time-series labels on the primary p95/tps metrics (too much cardinality when we scale models/regions).
- OK to attach gpu_sku/runtime_build/scheduler_mode as fields in the alert payload (derived from the “top contributors” query) or as exemplars/trace links.
- For the actual alerting query, I recommend labels limited to: model, region, traffic_source=perf-canary, stream_mode (yes/no), and maybe “slice_id” if we need a small fixed set of workload shapes.

If we do want GPU SKU splits, we should do it via a controlled enum (e.g., A100_80G/H100_80G/L40S) and only for a handful of models in phase 1. Otherwise we’ll be fighting the cardinality budget immediately.

I can update the Confluence metric spec example to match this (and add a note about payload enrichment vs labels).

Allison



From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>, Tomáš Novák <tomas.novak@redwoodinference.com>, Allison Grant <allison.grant@redwoodinference.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, Jan 11, 2026 at 4:48 PM PST
Subject: Re: Perf-canary alerting policy review (paging volume + phased rollout)

Works for me.

Implementation detail proposals:
- Create a dedicated PagerDuty service “perf-canary-regressions” with two routes:
  (a) WARN: webhook -> incident-bot post to #eng-oncall + create ticket, no PD incident
  (b) CRITICAL: create PD incident (SRE oncall) + incident-bot post + auto-link runbook + dashboards
- Dedup key: model|region|metric|severity as you suggested. We can include a “top_slice” field in the incident body (gpu_sku/runtime_build) without it affecting grouping.
- Maintenance windows: we can wire in suppression from the regression-detector side; PD doesn’t need to know the schedule.

If you want, I can open INT-3330 to get the PD service created + tested this week.

Rafael



From: Tomáš Novák <tomas.novak@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Allison Grant <allison.grant@redwoodinference.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Jan 12, 2026 at 8:17 AM PST
Subject: Re: Perf-canary alerting policy review (paging volume + phased rollout)

Agree with ticket-first.

Two things I want explicitly in the policy/runbook to keep paging hygiene:
1) “What to do first” checklist (5 minutes): verify sample size + check deploy annotations + compare to adjacent regions + confirm it’s not a canary restart/cold cache.
2) A rule that pages must include an actionable link set:
- dashboard (pre-filtered model/region)
- last runtime deploy + git sha
- runbook section anchor

Also: I like the “two consecutive windows” condition. We should document what a “window” means (e.g., 10m rollups, evaluated every 5m) so responders understand why it takes ~X minutes to fire.

Tomáš



From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>, Tomáš Novák <tomas.novak@redwoodinference.com>, Allison Grant <allison.grant@redwoodinference.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Jan 12, 2026 at 10:03 AM PST
Subject: Re: Perf-canary alerting policy review (paging volume + phased rollout)

Rafael — yes please open INT-3330 and proceed with the PD service.

For WARN: I’d prefer we still generate an “incident-looking” message in Slack (same template), but clearly marked “TICKET-FIRST (no page)”. That helps us evaluate whether the payload is sufficient.

All: I’ll update the policy doc today with:
- phased rollout
- ticket-first week 1
- CRITICAL-only paging week 2
- consecutive-window requirement
- suppression rules
- dedup key

I’ll also add Tomáš’s “what to do first” checklist to the runbook.

Sean



From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Tomáš Novák <tomas.novak@redwoodinference.com>, Allison Grant <allison.grant@redwoodinference.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jan 13, 2026 at 9:18 AM PST
Subject: Re: Perf-canary alerting policy review (paging volume + phased rollout)

Quick summary / decisions (so we’re aligned before implementation hardens):

Decisions
- Phase 1 (us-east, 2–3 models): run detectors in ticket-first mode for ~1 week.
- Phase 2: enable paging for CRITICAL only, same limited scope.
- Expand scope only after backtesting shows acceptable volume (target: <1 page/day) and payload is actionable.

Alert semantics
- WARN: ticket + #eng-oncall post (no PD). Thresholds TBD but starting point: p95 +10% / tps -8% sustained ~30m.
- CRITICAL: PD page. Starting point: p95 +15% / tps -12% sustained ~20m.
- Add “two consecutive windows” requirement except for extreme deltas (we’ll define that cutoff in the detector).

Cardinality
- Keep primary metrics low-cardinality (model/region/stream_mode/traffic_source).
- Enrich alert payload with gpu_sku/runtime_build/scheduler_mode/kernel selection from exemplars/top-slice query.

Next steps
- Rafael: INT-3330 -> PD service + routing (WARN vs CRITICAL) + incident-bot templates.
- Allison/Logan: confirm metric labels + payload enrichment pattern and update examples in spec.
- Sean (me): update Confluence alert policy + runbook checklist; link from detector repo.

If anything above is off, reply-all today so we don’t build the wrong thing.

Sean
—
Sean Gallagher
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
